items.followUp: Define a polyatomic ion and give one example.

rubric.why: A radical is a charged atom or group of atoms that behaves as one unit.
rubric.description: Defines a radical as charged and behaving as a single unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the charge and single-unit behaviour.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates knowledge of radicals.
rubric.description: Gives one valid example of a radical.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example, such as sulfate or ammonium.

modelAnswer: A radical is an atom or group of atoms carrying a positive or negative charge and behaving as a single unit in chemical reactions.

items.followUp: Name one radioactive isotope used as a medical tracer and state what it can help trace.

rubric.why: The isotopes used as tracers in medicine are radioactive isotopes.
rubric.description: Identifies the tracers as radioactive isotopes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as radioactive isotopes.

rubric.why: A named isotope provides a suitable example of a medical tracer.
rubric.description: Names one suitable isotope used as a medical tracer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example, such as sodium-24 or iodine-131.

modelAnswer: Radioactive isotopes are used as tracers in medicine.
Examples include sodium-24, which can trace blood circulation, and iodine-131, which can trace thyroid activity.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Each successive element down a group has an additional occupied electron shell.
rubric.description: States that an additional electron shell is present down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the addition of an electron shell down a group.

rubric.why: The additional shell places outer electrons farther from the nucleus and increases shielding, resulting in a larger atom.
rubric.description: Links the outer electrons' greater distance or shielding to increased atomic size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking greater distance from the nucleus or shielding to an increase in atomic size.

modelAnswer: Down a group, each successive element has an additional occupied electron shell.
The outer electrons are farther from the nucleus and experience greater shielding, so atomic size increases.
